report:
Your “no” is right only if “ensure” means guarantee: cortisone-like drugs do **not** ensure survival. But for critically ill COVID-19 patients who need oxygen or ventilation, dexamethasone **improves the chance** of survival and became standard care.

The pivotal RECOVERY randomized trial found lower 28-day mortality with dexamethasone among patients on invasive mechanical ventilation: 29.3% vs 41.4% with usual care (rate ratio 0.64), and among those receiving oxygen without ventilation: 23.3% vs 26.2% (rate ratio 0.82). It found **no benefit** in patients not needing respiratory support, with a trend toward harm. Source: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2021436

A WHO REACT meta-analysis of 7 randomized trials in critically ill patients likewise found systemic corticosteroids associated with lower 28-day all-cause mortality (about 32% vs 40%; odds ratio ~0.66). Source: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2770279

Guidelines therefore recommend dexamethasone 6 mg daily for up to 10 days for hospitalized patients requiring supplemental oxygen, noninvasive ventilation, or mechanical ventilation—not as a cure-all, and not for mild disease without oxygen need. Source: https://adsp.nm.org/uploads/1/4/3/0/143064172/nih_hosp_adult_guideline.pdf

Bottom line: dexamethasone does not guarantee survival, but in severe/critical COVID-19 with respiratory support it meaningfully reduces deaths; benefit depends on illness severity and timing.
